newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended stronger for the first trading day in five as German Bunds staged a rebound and the dollar finally came off its peak against the mark.
But the guilder yield curve steepened a little as investors reversed lengthening trades, taking profits realised during a marked flattening of the curve in recent weeks.
As has been the case for some time, trading volumes in Dutch state paper were light, a situation heightened by the summer holiday recess.
The September Bunds contract recovered after a bigger than expected increase in the German jobless total for July.
The number of unemployed rose a seasonally-adjusted 17,000 when analysts had forecast a 15,000 gain on average.
The high jobless rate in Germany and the low rate of inflation are thought to be limiting the Bundesbank's ability to increase money market rates to prop up the ailing mark.
Bund futures have been weak in recent days because of fears the German central bank would hike rates to support the currency against the dollar but they rebounded today.
"Technically, the market had been oversold," a London-based trader said, adding he did not expect the Bundesbank to act.
He attributed the fall in the dollar/mark to profit taking.
The trader said the market would perform well on Thursday if the U.S. auction of 10-year notes overnight was successful.
A dealer said investors took advantage of the market's strength to sell longer Dutch paper, particularly the 2023 state loan, and buy shorter dates, including 2000.
He said: "You saw some unwinding of flattening trades."
This strategy has paid dividend as the gap between short and long yields has fallen over the last month.
The dealer did not expect a rise in short German rates, a view echoed by another trader, who also noted buying interest in 2000 guilder paper.
